problems.title: GCD times LCM
problems.question: Find the product of the gcd and lcm of 24 and 36.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The gcd is 12 and lcm is 72. Their product is 864, also equal to 24×36.

problems.title: Recognize a binomial cube
problems.question: Simplify $a^3+3a^2b+3ab^2+b^3$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The four terms match the cube expansion exactly.

problems.title: Which radical expression is rational?
problems.question: Choose the rational expression: A $1/(\sqrt5+\sqrt2)+1/(\sqrt5-\sqrt2)$; B $1/(\sqrt7+2)-1/(\sqrt7-2)$; C $1/(4+\sqrt6)-1/(4-\sqrt6)$; D $1/(\sqrt5+2)+1/(\sqrt5-2)$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: A simplifies to $2\sqrt5/3$; B to $-4/3$; C to $-\sqrt6/5$; D to $2\sqrt5$.
Only B is rational.

problems.title: A leg from its hypotenuse projection
problems.question: In right triangle ABC, C is right and CH is an altitude. BH=1,BC=3. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.

problems.title: Tangent and bisected secant
problems.question: A tangent from an exterior point has length √2. A secant segment from that point to the farther intersection is divided into two equal parts at the nearer intersection. Find its total length.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: Tangent squared = external secant part × whole secant.
steps: Let each equal part be t. Then $2=t(2t)$, giving t=1. The whole secant is 2t=2.

problems.title: Zeros after taking absolute value
problems.question: The roots of f(x)=0 are {−3,−2,1}. Find the roots of |f(x)|=0.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Taking an absolute value preserves exactly the zero values.

problems.title: Parallel line slopes
problems.question: Which listed line is parallel to the line through (1,4) and (−3,0)?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The slope is 1. The listed line y=x−2 has slope 1; the other choices do not.

problems.title: Locate a logarithm without a calculator
problems.question: Which listed interval contains log base 3 of 25?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The base-3 logarithm increases, so $2<\log_325<3$.

problems.title: Supplementary angles and percentages
problems.question: 15% of one supplementary angle equals 45% of the other. Find the smaller angle.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The second equation gives u=3v. Thus 4v=180°, so the smaller angle is 45°.

problems.title: Count a prism’s vertices, faces and edges
problems.question: Which of 600,601,602,603 can be the sum of all vertex, face and edge counts of a prism?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: An n-gonal prism has V=2n,F=n+2,E=3n, total 6n+2.
steps: The total must be 2 modulo 6. Only 602 has this form, giving n=100, a valid polygonal base.

problems.title: Range of a quadratic
problems.question: Find the range of $2x^2+4x+3$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The squared term is nonnegative and can take every value from zero upward. The minimum is 1 at x=−1.

problems.title: Add exponential parameters
problems.question: $4^a=28$ and $2^b=1/\sqrt7$. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.

problems.title: A nested logarithm
problems.question: Solve $\log_2(\log_2x)=1+\log_25$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Injectivity gives log₂x=10, then x=2¹⁰. It satisfies the nested-log domain x>1.

problems.title: Circumradius with a one-to-two-to-six angle ratio
problems.question: Triangle angles are in ratio 1:2:6 and its longest side is 5. Find its circumradius.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The angles are 20°,40°,120°. The longest side 5 is opposite 120°, so $R=5/(2\sin120^\circ)=5/\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Area in a unit square with two midpoints
problems.question: ABCD is a unit square; M is midpoint of AD and N midpoint of BM. Find area CDMN.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: Shoelace formula: $S=\tfrac12|\sum x_i y_{i+1}-\sum y_i x_{i+1}|$.
steps: For C,D,M,N the forward sum is 1+0+0+1/2=3/2; the reverse sum is 0+0+1/4+1/4=1/2. Half their difference is 1/2.

problems.title: A quotient of common logarithms
problems.question: Simplify $((\lg19)^2-1)/\lg190$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Cancel the nonzero factor lg19+1. The quotient is lg19−1=lg(19/10)=lg1.9.

problems.title: An equation that is an identity
problems.question: How many solutions in $(0,\pi/2)$ satisfy $(2^{\sin x})^{\sin x}\,2^{\cos^2x}=2$?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The left side is $2^{\sin^2x}2^{\cos^2x}=2^1=2$. Every x in the interval works.
problems.answer: Infinitely many; every point of the interval.

problems.title: Combine logarithms with a positive domain
problems.question: Solve $\log_2x+\log_2(x^2)=1$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: The domain is x>0; the sum is $\log_2(x^3)$.
steps: x³=2, so x=∛2, which is positive and valid.

problems.title: Lateral area of a right triangular prism
problems.question: A right prism has a 3:4 right-triangle base. Its height equals the median to the hypotenuse. Volume is 120 cm³. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: Write legs 3t,4t, hypotenuse 5t, height 5t/2. $V=B h$; lateral area $=P h$.
steps: Base area is 6t², so volume is 15t³=120 and t=2.
The perimeter is 12t=24 and height 5. Lateral area is 120 cm².

problems.title: Inclination of a cube diagonal
problems.question: Find the angle between space diagonal AC₁ and base ABCD of a cube.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: For cube side s, the height is s and base diagonal projection is s√2. Therefore tan theta=1/√2.

problems.title: Count integer exponents
problems.question: How many integer x satisfy $0.9<2^x<100$?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The allowed integer exponents are 0,1,2,3,4,5,6, giving seven.

problems.title: An impossible logarithmic inequality
problems.question: Solve $\log_{10}(\sin x)>0$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: For base 10, log t>0 iff t>1.
steps: The inequality would require sin x>1, impossible. Inputs with nonpositive sine are also outside the logarithm domain.

problems.title: A downward quadratic from a positivity interval
problems.question: $-x^2+ax+b>0$ has solution interval (−7,4). Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Expanding gives $-x^2-3x+28$. Thus a=−3,b=28 and their sum is 25.

problems.title: Pyramid edge and face counts
problems.question: A regular pyramid has six more edges than faces. Find its number of edges.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: With n base sides, E=2n and F=n+1.
steps: $2n-(n+1)=6$ gives n=7, hence E=14.

problems.title: Total area of a square prism
problems.question: A regular square prism has height 2 cm and base diagonal 5√2 cm. Find its total surface area.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: s=5, so the total area is 50+40=90 cm².

problems.title: Order three logarithms
problems.question: Order $a=\log_52,b=\log_25,c=\log_53$ increasingly.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Since 1<2<3<5, we have 0<a<c<1. Meanwhile b>1.

problems.title: Mass in a rectangular tank
problems.question: A 2 m by 4 m by 1 m tank is full. Each litre of its liquid weighs 0.8 kg. Find the total mass.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: Volume $=lwh$; $1\text{ m}^3=1000$ litres; mass = volume × mass per litre.
steps: The volume is 8 m³=8000 litres. The mass is 8000×0.8=6400 kg.

problems.title: Volume of an equilateral triangular prism
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side 1. The two base areas together equal its lateral area. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: $3h=2B=\sqrt3/2$, giving $h=\sqrt3/6$. The volume is $(\sqrt3/4)(\sqrt3/6)=1/8$.

problems.title: A logarithmic inequality with its domain
problems.question: Solve $\log_2(2x+3)<1$.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The domain gives x>−3/2 and the upper inequality gives x<−1/2. Both are strict.

problems.title: An obtuse angle with integer side lengths
problems.question: An obtuse triangle has integer sides. The sides adjacent to its obtuse angle are 3 and 4. Find that angle’s cosine.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: For opposite side c, triangle inequality gives c<7; obtuseness gives c²>3²+4²=25.
steps: Thus 5<c<7 and integer c must be 6. The cosine rule gives $(9+16-36)/(2\cdot3\cdot4)=-11/24$.

problems.title: Speeds from a per-kilometre time difference
problems.question: A train travels twice as fast as a car and takes 20 seconds less per kilometre. Find both speeds.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: Let car speed be v km/h. Time per km in seconds is 3600/v.
steps: The train speed is 2v, so $3600/v-3600/(2v)=20$. Thus 1800/v=20 and v=90.
The train speed is 180 km/h.

problems.title: Dihedral angle of a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: A triangular pyramid has all six edges equal. Find the cosine of its internal dihedral angle.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
formulas: Cut perpendicular to a shared edge through its midpoint M. The cross-section uses the two face altitudes.
steps: For edge length s, these altitudes have lengths s√3/2; the distance between their other endpoints is s.
The cosine rule gives $\cos\theta=[2(3s^2/4)-s^2]/[2(3s^2/4)]=1/3$.

problems.title: Product of two hundred geometric terms
problems.question: For every natural n, $\log_3(2S_n+1)=n$. Find the product of the first 200 sequence terms.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Using S₀=0 gives $b_n=3^{n-1}$. The product is $3^{0+1+\cdots+199}$.
The exponent sum is 199×200/2=19900.

problems.title: Parameters outside an exponential range
problems.question: For which real k does $3^{x+2}-2\cdot3^x+1=k$ have no real solution?
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: The left side is $7\cdot3^x+1$, with range (1,∞). It takes each value greater than 1 once and never reaches 1.
Therefore no solution exists exactly for k≤1.

problems.title: Largest total area with a fixed sum of prism edges
problems.question: A regular triangular prism’s nine edges total 18. Find its greatest possible total surface area.
problems.idea: Use a standard identity or geometric relationship, then verify the permitted values.
steps: Write h=6−2a, with 0<a<3. Then $S=18a-(6-\sqrt3/2)a^2$.
For C=6−√3/2>0, this is $81/C-C(a-9/C)^2$. The maximizing a=9/C lies between 0 and 3, so h is positive.
The maximum is $81/C=162/(12-\sqrt3)=54(12+\sqrt3)/47$.
